s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive vertigo with severe headaches and nausea, associated with a cerebellar mass and surrounding edema
salient_findings: Severe bifrontal throbbing headaches with nausea and vomiting
Positive right-sided Dix-Hallpike maneuver with horizontal nystagmus
3 cm left cerebellar hemispheric mass with surrounding vasogenic edema
key_facts: 74-year-old man with a history of metastatic prostate cancer
Known left upper lobe lung mass
Four weeks of progressive vertigo
Severe bifrontal throbbing headaches with nausea and vomiting
Positive for adenovirus at an outside emergency department
No focal motor or sensory deficits on neurologic examination
Intact coordination on dysdiadochokinesia, finger-to-nose, and heel-to-shin testing
Intact gait despite dizziness
Positive right-sided Dix-Hallpike maneuver with horizontal nystagmus
Noncontrast head CT showed a 3 cm left cerebellar hemispheric mass
MRI of the brain demonstrated a cystic enhancing lesion in the left cerebellar hemisphere
Cerebral angiography revealed no abnormal hyperemia at the site of the lesion
